content:
Over the past year, many have been eagerly awaiting the arrival of the next-generation iPad mini, and multiple sources suggest its release is imminent. New information leaked by Aaron Perris last week shows the new device will feature an A20 Pro chip and narrower screen bezels; additionally, we already know it will come with an OLED display and a waterproof design.

While these upgrades are indeed appealing, my main expectation for the next-generation iPad mini actually lies in the software.

After seeing iPhone Duo, I was truly amazed by Apple's approach to multitasking. To me, multitasking on the iPad has always been a mess, but iPhone Duo handles it with elegance and fluidity.

On such a small screen, the iPad mini has never really been suited for windowed mode. Users rarely stack multiple windows on the iPad mini. So I hope they can borrow from iPhone Duo and add a practical feature: split view with picture-in-picture.

Top-rated comment posted by MATTHEW LEBER

You make a good point, and you've hit on my biggest complaint; the software on iPad mini is just a shrunken version of the larger iPad. Apple doesn't seem to have put much thought into tailoring the experience for this screen size. The home screen widgets are so small they're barely legible, and the number of app icon rows you can place is very limited, wasting a lot of empty space. The whole experience is really poor.

Honestly, this experience could be much better. Currently on iPad mini, the picture-in-picture window cannot occupy the full screen width in portrait mode; even if it could, you still have to cover part of the app, or manually resize the window yourself.

To me, bringing split-screen video and app views to the iPad mini's screen is almost a given, especially since the aspect ratios of the iPhone Duo and iPad mini screens are so similar. With this feature, I'd at least be more willing to use the iPad mini in portrait mode.
